page: Vultr voc-c-2c-4gb-50s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core and 2 threads. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of RAM, translating to 2.0 GB per core, and includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, AES, and SHA_NI.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top tier (top 10%) and Geekbench single-core scores in the top 25%. Single-threaded operations like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also perform strongly. However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks show limitations. Geekbench multi-core, Passmark CPU, and Passmark database operations fall into the bottom 25%, while static web serving throughput is in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, but small-block cached read bandwidth is weak.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources paired with fast local NVMe storage, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads that require reliable single-core performance without massive memory footprints. Due to the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lower multi-core benchmark results, it is suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, text processing, basic software compilation, or small-scale development environments rather than high-throughput web serving, large databases, or memory-heavy applications.
